name: Accordion
description: A vertically stacked set of interactive headings that each contain a title representing a section of content. Users can expand or collapse associated content panels.

keyboard_interactions.action: Expands collapsed panel; may collapse other panels if only one can be expanded

Moves focus to next focusable element in page tab sequence
Moves focus to previous focusable element in page tab sequence
(Optional) Moves focus to next accordion header; wraps from last to first
(Optional) Moves focus to previous accordion header; wraps from first to last
(Optional) Moves focus to first accordion header
(Optional) Moves focus to last accordion header

roles.description: Applied to each accordion header title element
Wraps the button element with appropriate aria-level

required_attributes.description: State. On the header BUTTON, never on the panel or the heading.
References the ID of the associated panel content element
Only needed when faking a heading with role='heading'. Use a real <h2>-<h6> instead and this disappears.

optional_attributes.description: true when the panel is visible and cannot be collapsed
References the ID of the header button that controls the panel

notes: Prefer a native <button> wrapped in a real heading element (<h2>-<h6>) over role='heading' + aria-level.
The heading wraps the button. The button does NOT wrap the heading, and the heading is not the control.
Pick the heading level from the surrounding document outline, not from the accordion's own nesting.
Hide collapsed panels with the `hidden` attribute or display:none — never opacity or clipping (RAWeb 10.8).
Arrow-key navigation between headers is OPTIONAL. If you add it, Tab must still move through headers normally — arrows are an accelerator, not a replacement.
For an exclusive accordion (one panel at a time), native <details name='group'> does it with zero JS.
role='region' on each panel is only worth it for a small number of panels; on a long accordion it floods the landmark list.

raweb_criteria.reason: Each header button must expose its expanded/collapsed state via aria-expanded.
Headers must be real buttons so Enter/Space work; optional arrow-key navigation must not replace Tab.
Accordion headers are headings. Wrap each button in a real h2-h6 at the level the document structure calls for, so the accordion appears in the heading outline a screen reader user navigates by.
Each header must show a visible focus indicator.
Collapsed panels must be hidden from assistive technologies, not just visually.
